method: Cataclysm-only mechanics were located from string literals (beastweapon.script/scriptStructEntry table, english.script key pointers resolved through the language scriptEntry table {name,0x528800,&char*} so code that prints a key can be found by its global, debug format strings, SALVAGING:* errors, fow*/FOW* names) and from callers of already-named HW1/CET functions (univCreateShip, GetShipStaticInfo, gunShoot, rmUpdateResearch, MothershipSpecialTarget...) that have no HW1 counterpart. Every candidate's Ghidra decompile was read; struct offsets were matched to CET's reconstructed Ship/ShipStaticInfo/Player fields (beastAttackCascadeCost 0x3DC, beastAttacksRequired 0x3E0, fowRadius 0x240, supportUnits 0x410, providesSU 0x414, upgradeTimeModifier 0x1F8, beastSystemType 0x650, Player supportUnitsMax/Used 0xC/0x10) and ship-type ids to CET ShipDefs.h; tech ids come from the exe's {id,"TECH_*"} table at 0x8901A8. Rel32 call scans of cataclysm.exe recovered callers the call graph missed. Only function entries present in functions.csv are proposed; names already proposed by other files were not re-proposed unless noted. Confidence: high = string or CET-field evidence plus consistent callers; medium = behaviour read from the decompile with one corroborating caller; low = role inferred.
